title: Here is What to Know Beyond Why Spotify Technology (SPOT) is a Trending Stock

Here is What to Know Beyond Why Spotify Technology (SPOT) is a Trending Stock

Spotify (SPOT) has been one of the most searched-for stocks on Zacks.com lately. So, you might want to look at some of the facts that could shape the stock's performance in the near term.

Over the past month, shares of this music-streaming service operator have returned +16.3%, compared to the Zacks S&P 500 composite's -2.4% change. During this period, the Zacks Internet - Software industry, which Spotify falls in, has lost 10.6%. The key question now is: What could be the stock's future direction?

Although media reports or rumors about a significant change in a company's business prospects usually cause its stock to trend and lead to an immediate price change, there are always certain fundamental factors that ultimately drive the buy-and-hold decision.

Earnings Estimate Revisions

Here at Zacks, we prioritize appraising the change in the projection of a company's future earnings over anything else. That's because we believe the present value of its future stream of earnings is what determines the fair value for its stock.

We essentially look at how sell-side analysts covering the stock are revising their earnings estimates to reflect the impact of the latest business trends. And if earnings estimates go up for a company, the fair value for its stock goes up. A higher fair value than the current market price drives investors' interest in buying the stock, leading to its price moving higher. This is why empirical research shows a strong correlation between trends in earnings estimate revisions and near-term stock price movements.

For the current quarter, Spotify is expected to post earnings of $3.71 per share, indicating a change of -28.1% from the year-ago quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate has changed +0.7% over the last 30 days.

The consensus earnings estimate of $13.6 for the current fiscal year indicates a year-over-year change of +14.4%. This estimate has changed -1.2% over the last 30 days.

For the next fiscal year, the consensus earnings estimate of $15.86 indicates a change of +16.6% from what Spotify is expected to report a year ago. Over the past month, the estimate has changed -8.6%.

Having a strong externally audited track record, our proprietary stock rating tool, the Zacks Rank, offers a more conclusive picture of a stock's price direction in the near term, since it effectively harnesses the power of earnings estimate revisions. Due to the size of the recent change in the consensus estimate, along with three other factors related to earnings estimates, Spotify is rated Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

title: Is Spotify (SPOT) a Buy as Wall Street Analysts Look Optimistic?

Is Spotify (SPOT) a Buy as Wall Street Analysts Look Optimistic?
Zacks Equity Research
Mon, November 9, 2026 at 5:30 AM PST 4 min read
SPOT
Trade SPOT on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Investors often turn to recommendations made by Wall Street analysts before making a Buy, Sell, or Hold decision about a stock. While media reports about rating changes by these brokerage-firm employed (or sell-side) analysts often affect a stock's price, do they really matter?

Before we discuss the reliability of brokerage recommendations and how to use them to your advantage, let's see what these Wall Street heavyweights think about Spotify (SPOT).

Spotify currently has an average brokerage recommendation (ABR) of 1.76, on a scale of 1 to 5 (Strong Buy to Strong Sell), calculated based on the actual recommendations (Buy, Hold, Sell, etc.) made by 35 brokerage firms. An ABR of 1.76 approximates between Strong Buy and Buy.

Of the 35 recommendations that derive the current ABR, 21 are Strong Buy and three are Buy. Strong Buy and Buy respectively account for 60% and 8.6% of all recommendations.

Brokerage Recommendation Trends for SPOT
Broker Rating Breakdown Chart for SPOT

Check price target & stock forecast for Spotify here>>>

While the ABR calls for buying Spotify, it may not be wise to make an investment decision solely based on this information. Several studies have shown limited to no success of brokerage recommendations in guiding investors to pick stocks with the best price increase potential.

Are you wondering why? The vested interest of brokerage firms in a stock they cover often results in a strong positive bias of their analysts in rating it. Our research shows that for every "Strong Sell" recommendation, brokerage firms assign five "Strong Buy" recommendations.

This means that the interests of these institutions are not always aligned with those of retail investors, giving little insight into the direction of a stock's future price movement. It would therefore be best to use this information to validate your own analysis or a tool that has proven to be highly effective at predicting stock price movements.

Zacks Rank, our proprietary stock rating tool with an impressive externally audited track record, categorizes stocks into five groups, ranging from Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) to Zacks Rank #5 (Strong Sell), and is an effective indicator of a stock's price performance in the near future. Therefore, using the ABR to validate the Zacks Rank could be an efficient way of making a profitable investment decision.

Zacks Rank Should Not Be Confused With ABR

In spite of the fact that Zacks Rank and ABR both appear on a scale from 1 to 5, they are two completely different measures.

Broker recommendations are the sole basis for calculating the ABR, which is typically displayed in decimals (such as 1.28). The Zacks Rank, on the other hand, is a quantitative model designed to harness the power of earnings estimate revisions. It is displayed in whole numbers -- 1 to 5.

title: Spotify Just Gained 7% in a Week. What Will It Take to Hit $700?
detail:

Aditya Raghunath
November 6, 2026 4 min read

Spotify Just Gained 7% in a Week. What Will It Take to Hit $700? ©@twinsterphoto via Canva; @Adam Smigielski from Getty Images Signature via Canva
Key Takeaways

Spotify (SPOT:NYSE) stock is up 7% in the past week, mostly after a report that it plans a paid AI remix and cover service for early 2027, possibly at $4 to $5 a month extra.

The add-on would let Spotify charge for AI just as growth in Premium revenue per user slows after its price increases.

Analysts already expect normalized earnings per share to rise about 45% from 2025 to 2027, and the remix service isn't in those estimates.

JP Morgan and Morgan Stanley recently raised the target price to $700. This works out to about 44x expected earnings, below the stock's average since early 2024, so reaching it depends mainly on the Q4 report in early February.

Spotify is up 7% in the past week. Over the same stretch, the Nasdaq 100 fell 7%, and the S&P 500 slipped 5%. As of Thursday's close, the stock sits about 4% below its 52-week high.

$700 is about 14% above that close. Getting there would take two things: a new way to charge subscribers, and a strong holiday quarter.

What exactly happened

The biggest gain came on Friday, Oct. 30. Early that morning, the Financial Times reported that Spotify plans a paid AI service for remixes and covers:

Timing: Q1 of 2027, possibly around the Grammy Awards in February

Price: possibly $4 to $5 a month on top of a subscription

Labels: Universal Music Group, indie-label group Merlin and Believe have signed on, while Sony Music and Warner Music are still negotiating

On Monday, Citi raised its target to $715 from $620 and kept its Buy rating. Wednesday's gain came with no company news, as internet stocks rallied with the market.

TIKR tracks 41 analysts on Spotify. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Spotify, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Spotify's Analyst Ratings

A new way to charge more

Spotify could use one. Its Q3 beat its own guidance on Oct. 22, and price increases did much of the work: Premium revenue grew 17% to €4.49 billion while subscribers grew 9%.

That boost is fading. Premium revenue per user rose 7.5% at constant currency in Q3. For Q4, management guides 4.5% to 5% as Spotify laps price increases in more than 150 markets.

At $4 to $5, the remix add-on would cost roughly a third as much as the $12.99 US individual plan. It would also have Spotify making money from AI, which investors have mostly treated as a threat.

Last month, Jefferies analyst James Heaney called the platform "highly defensible against AI disintermediation fears." The add-on goes further: subscribers would pay extra for the AI itself.

title: Spotify Is Up 33% in Six Months: Take Profits, or Buy More?
detail:
Spotify Is Up 33% in Six Months: Take Profits, or Buy More?
Rexielyn Diaz
November 1, 2026 5 min read
SPOT
Trade SPOT on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Spotify Is Up 33% in Six Months: Take Profits, or Buy More? ©twinsterphoto and Eugenio Marongiu via Canva
Key Takeaways

Spotify jumped 6.5% on Friday to $593 and is up 33% in six months, as Universal Music reported a subscription beat the same day.

Third-quarter operating income of €672 million beat guidance, and co-CEO Alex Norström said "this was a quarter where we did what we said."

Fourth-quarter guidance needs 10 million net subscriber adds and a 15.8% operating margin, both well above what the third quarter delivered.

The stock trades at 37.5x forward earnings with a $642 average target, so the February report has to confirm the margin step-up.

In July, Spotify stock was down about 16% for the year. Investors were punishing it for spending.

That mood is gone. Spotify (SPOT:NYSE) jumped 6.5% on Friday to close at $593, and it is now up 33% over six months. The stock sits about 11% below its 52-week high of $669.

Friday's move came as Universal Music Group (UMG), the world's biggest record label, reported subscription growth that beat expectations. That's a reversal for UMG, whose stock fell about 25% in July when its underlying subscription growth missed. On the same day, the Financial Times reported that Spotify is aiming for a 2027 launch of an AI remix service.

Those stories connect. Spotify and UMG signed licensing deals in May covering fan-made covers and remixes, the groundwork any remix product needs.

So at $593, do you take profits or buy more?

A quarter of small beats

Spotify's third quarter, reported October 22, edged past its own guidance almost everywhere.

Revenue rose 16% to €4.97 billion, or 14% in constant currency.

Gross margin hit a third-quarter record of 33.0%, up 136 basis points.

Premium subscribers reached 306 million on 6 million net adds, 1 million above guidance.

Operating income of €672 million topped the €670 million guide as marketing and personnel costs came in light. "This was a quarter where we did what we said," co-CEO Alex Norström said in the results release.

Net income fell 42% to €518 million, but that drop sits below the operating line. The year-ago quarter carried €197 million of gains on since-repaid exchangeable notes plus a tax benefit.

Gross margin is the trend that matters…

Spotify Technology (SPOT): gross margin (%), quarterly, Q3 2024–Q3 2026 (TIKR)

Management guided fourth-quarter gross margin to 33.8%, so the climb isn't finished.

Pricing is doing the lifting

Premium revenue grew 17% to €4.49 billion, well ahead of 9% subscriber growth. Price increases and add-ons like Audiobooks+ fill that gap.

That's faster growth than the labels Spotify pays. Its Premium revenue grew 15% in constant currency last quarter, more than double the 6.7% underlying subscription growth UMG posted in its second quarter.
